sections.title: Guides for the applications and native system

items.title: Using sources and recurring programs

sections.headline: Three concrete checks *for an existing Wix site.*
sections.lede: Prepared in response to a public request for technical SEO work. This is an independent review of the pages anyone can load. It is not a client engagement, a Search Console inspection or a claim about rankings.

items.title: Search intent is diluted
items.text: The delivered title leads with “elite accreditation services review”, and the page has a second primary heading phrased as a review. A service buyer is more directly served by a title such as “Healthcare Accreditation Consultants | Elite Accreditation” and a service-led introduction.

items.title: The same long introduction repeats
items.text: Several testimonial blocks carry the same broad service-description paragraphs. Make each testimonial concise, keep one authoritative service introduction, and link to the specific service pages instead of repeating the same text.

items.title: The HTML response is 2,320,224 bytes
items.text: That is the uncompressed response-body size observed in this run, not a Core Web Vitals score. Inspect Wix apps, video embeds and repeated sections, then measure mobile loading before and after each change.

sections.title: What was inspected
sections.caveat: A reachable sitemap is not proof of Google indexing. “Discovered, not indexed” and “Crawled, not indexed” need their actual URL examples and Search Console evidence before assigning a cause.

sections.title: A first implementation pass — without a platform migration

items.title: Baseline
items.text: Record current Wix settings and selected service pages, then inspect Search Console examples with owner-approved read access.

items.title: Correct high-intent pages
items.text: Refine homepage and key ASC/DME service titles, headings and internal links, preserving the site and its existing content ownership.

items.title: Measure the change
items.text: Recheck rendered pages and crawlability; track indexing and qualified enquiries separately. No paid backlinks or ranking guarantees.

pages.title: A training app for a studio

sections.headline: One training app. *Every studio its own.*
sections.lede: A sample built for a strength studio and a yoga studio. Members train from their phone, coaches write and publish the programmes, and each studio keeps its own name, colours and typeface. The studios and members shown here are made up.

items.title: Answer requests
items.text: A member asks for a programme. The coach picks the request up, drafts a plan and sends it back to that member.

items.text: A programme is reviewed before it goes out. Each change is a new version, and a programme can be withdrawn.

items.title: Set the studio’s look
items.text: Name, colours, typeface and mark are set in one place and the member app follows.

items.title: Review a workout from your watch
items.text: Choose a TCX workout file from an app that supports export. Review its duration, distance and heart rate before adding it to your history. Apple Watch and Wear OS exports use the same review.

items.title: Put your plan on your calendar
items.text: Share upcoming sessions with a calendar app or download the calendar file, even offline. Each session is an all-day event. Calendar copies do not update when your plan changes.

items.title: Connect a heart-rate sensor
items.text: Pair a compatible Bluetooth heart-rate sensor in a supported browser and choose whether to save readings with your workout. Physical-device checks are still pending. Direct Apple Health and Health Connect sync and watch controls are not available yet.

pages.title: Shared catalogue, room and audio workspaces

sections.headline: Continue the same work together.
sections.lede: Use the specialized catalogue, room and audio editors with destination-owned drafts. Keep original browser work and choose explicitly where to adopt it.

sections.title: Install and open the right editor

items.title: Choose a destination
items.text: In Aurekai setup choose Catalogue, Room Planning or Audio Studio — shared workspace. Select your personal workspace, an organization you administer, or a household where you are steward or delegated admin.

items.title: Install, then activate
items.text: Installation pins the reviewed behavior and creates native backend bindings. Activate separately, then open the specialized editor. Published source material stays shared; saved drafts belong to this destination.

items.title: Continue saved work
items.text: Catalogue selections open in the room editor with the same plan, fixture and model identities. Audio sessions retain their original WAV sources and clip edits. Another authorized member can reopen the saved work; stale overwrites are refused.

items.title: Review an existing account
items.text: The recorded steward opens Household access from the selected configuration, enters an existing account email, and reviews the member before changing access. This does not create accounts or send invitations.

items.title: Choose the access
items.text: Read allows inspection, write allows shared draft edits, and admin allows configuration changes. Only the steward manages memberships. Personal training records and other households stay separate.

items.title: Remove access, keep the work
items.text: Choose none to revoke a member. Saved work remains; expired and revoked grants are refused on the next request. Changing a steward away and back cannot revive an old grant. Browser expiry renewal remains separate.

items.title: Select at the source
items.text: Choose Bring browser drafts in the native editor. Spaces offers Work Samples or GitHub Spaces; audio offers Work Samples audio. In the source window choose the saved drafts and needed files, then send that selection for review.

items.title: Review the destination
items.text: New drafts are offered. Different existing drafts are not selected automatically; choose replacements deliberately. A concurrent member edit invalidates a stale review. Originals and their browser revisions stay unchanged.

items.title: Retain identities, review permissions
items.text: Plans keep fixture identities, but imported submission receipts are cleared. Audio keeps original recordings and clip coordinates; recipient recording permission resets to unreviewed. Reload the editor after adoption.

items.title: Native persistence
items.text: Atomic revision-checked saves and verified binary sources never silently fall back to a different browser-local draft. Deactivation preserves work. Uploads remain bounded; automatic abandoned-upload reclamation is still open.

items.title: Still separate
items.text: Training, Brief Studio and ITAD need their own backend adaptations. WAV export is not channel delivery. Supplier ordering and merchant publication are not implemented by this release.

items.title: Verification
items.text: The follow-up passes 25 household access checks, 20 audio browser checks and eight two-origin audio adoption checks. Adoption also passes from the actual public Work Samples source into an isolated native account, including reopening the waveform editor. Live public setup and access refusals pass on all four Aurekai domains. No production test account was created.
